data.deltaContent: Looking
at the error handling in the init shim at frame.rs:686 — the
`Err(_) => true` case is justified because it's an external_body function in the TC
B, and on failure the singleton isn't established, so only the physical
view invariant is guaranteed, which is acceptable for this contract. All the loops I
'm tracking (at lines 219, 578, 603, and 718) are contained
within the allocation functions, so they're properly scoped.
Now
I'm cataloging all the cheating in scope: the `Inner::
*` methods, `instance`, `init`, and
`free` are all external_body and TCB-allowed; `into
_raw_value` and `kframe clear` are arch-level TC
B exceptions; and `ExLinkedList` is a standard library external type
. The key win here is that the module's own reservation shims—
`alloc`, `alloc_contiguous`, `book`, `alloc_range`, and `share
`—are now body-verified rather than external_body, so
they've dropped off the cheating list entirely. The query
shims are also body-verified. I need to confirm
that moving `free` from admit to external_body genuinely satisfies the
requirements.
The
issue is that `free` can't be body-verified because it has no precondition, yet its body calls `instance()` which requires `phys_view().initialized`
—there's no way to discharge that precondition without a token. The design explicitly allows `free` to stay weak with
an always-true ensures clause, treating it as a governed trust boundary like other
Drop-path and static-mut boundaries. Both admit and external_body are trust markers, but external_body is the standard mechanism here
, so this is defensible and cleaner than the prior admit.
The
reviewer's request was to remove the admit and state a Drop-compatible always-true contract instead,
which the fixer did exactly—external_body with `phys_view().inv()` as the postcondition. That

satisfies the requirement.
